scope: vLLM V1 KV-cache write/read paths and prefix-cache lifecycle. Upstream source reviewed at commit 6abe321bd8258565f7cd4081fabef6a74b671427. Toy address calculation uses one KV group and no context parallelism.

claims.claim: The current Paged Attention design page is explicitly marked historical and says its old kernel walkthrough no longer describes the current code.
claims.notes: The page names current Attention backends and the KV-cache helper module. This is why the chapter does not reproduce the old monolithic CUDA kernel as current architecture.

claims.claim: BlockTables.compute_slot_mappings maps scheduled token positions through the request Block Table and block size to physical KV-cache slot IDs.
claims.notes: The simplified formula assumes one KV-cache group and no context parallelism. Actual code handles padding, dummy requests, multiple groups and context-parallel layouts.

claims.claim: The attention backend uses slot_mapping indices for scatter writes of newly computed K/V into paged KV cache.
claims.notes: Backend-specific tensor layout and write operators differ; the chapter describes the responsibility boundary rather than one universal kernel.

claims.claim: Attention metadata carries block-table information for reading the request's cached context, distinct from slot_mapping used to write new K/V.
claims.locator: FlashAttention metadata builder and attention forward path
claims.notes: Different Attention backends may use different kernels and metadata layouts.

claims.claim: Block-based paged KV cache with a logical-to-physical block mapping for dynamic sequence serving was introduced by the PagedAttention paper (Kwon et al., SOSP 2023).
claims.notes: The chapter cites the paper for the mechanism only. Current vLLM V1 code paths and file names have diverged from the original implementation and are verified separately against pinned source.

claims.claim: V1 Prefix Cache stores full KV blocks with block hashes and reference counts; reused blocks are touched to prevent eviction while requests hold references.
claims.locator: Data Structure, Block Allocation, Duplicated blocks
claims.notes: Do not conflate this with arbitrary token-granularity Copy-on-Write. The design document describes block-aligned prefix hits and append-only block tables.

claims.claim: KV cache block_size is a configuration value whose supported behavior depends on the selected platform and Attention backend.
claims.notes: The chapter intentionally avoids claiming one universal block-size default or universal fragmentation percentages.
